land.text: the Northern Zhou realm, which Emperor Jing of Northern Zhou handed to Yang Jian on 4 March 581

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps its Northern Zhou row to 586 and starts the Sui at 587; the Sui of 581-586 is drawn from the Northern Zhou 577 shape (new keyframe sui-dynasty_581).

land.text: Jiangling and the Western Liang territory in central Hubei

predecessors.note: The Sui infobox lists the Western Liang as a predecessor; it was a puppet state until 587, so it is a gain event of 587, not a birth handover.

land.text: the Chen realm south of the Yangtze, taken in 589

predecessors.note: The Sui infobox lists the Chen as a predecessor; the land came in 589 (gain event), not at birth.

land.text: Chang'an, taken by Li Yuan in winter 617, and the Tang founded there in 618; the Tang then took most of the Sui empire from the rival regimes by 628

successors.note: Infobox: 'Abolished by Li Yuan: 23 May 618 AD'; successor Tang dynasty. The Tang's own start is in the Tang dossier.

land.text: Luoyang, where Yang Tong's Sui yielded to Wang Shichong in summer 619

successors.note: The last Sui regime. Wang Shichong's Zheng (619-621) is a rebel-type dossier written in this batch.

capitals.name: Daxing (Chang'an, Xi'an)
capitals.note: Infobox: Daxing 581-605. Li Yuan took the city in winter 617 and made Yang You emperor there.

capitals.name: Luoyang
capitals.note: Infobox: Luoyang 605-618; the Emperor Yang page says he decided in winter 604 to make it the 'eastern capital'. Emperor Yang lived at Jiangdu (Yangzhou) from fall 616, which 'effectively became a third capital' in 610; Yang Tong's regime held Luoyang to 619.

rulers.name: Emperor Yang (Yang Guang)
rulers.note: The infobox gives 604-617, the reign table 604-618; killed at Jiangdu in spring 618.

rulers.name: Emperor Gong (Yang You)
rulers.note: Set up by Li Yuan at Chang'an in winter 617; deposed when Li Yuan founded the Tang.

rulers.name: Emperor Gong (Yang Tong)
rulers.note: Proclaimed at Luoyang after Emperor Yang's death; 'legitimacy more recognized by historians but still disputed'; yielded to Wang Shichong in summer 619.

correction.text: the Northern Zhou realm as Yang Jian received it in 581

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 581-586. Cliopatria's Sui row starts in 587 and draws the Northern Zhou 577 shape (1.77 M km2; Northern Zhou infobox 1.5 M km2 in 577) until 586, but Yang Jian ascended on 4 March 581 and 'usurped the throne from the Northern Zhou rulers'. Same land, new state from 581.

Shape unchanged, but it holds only 587-588: the Sui took Chen in Feb 589, and Cliopatria's next shape (592) really begins in 589. 2.02 M km2 = the Northern Zhou 577 shape + the Later Western Liang (abolished 587, 'Disestablished 587 AD', Western Liang page) + about 0.22 M km2 of Ordos, northern Shanxi and northern Hebei that no page opened here assigns to the Sui before 617. Infobox area 3.0 M km2 is for 589 (see next verdict). [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 587..588 from this entry's own 'valid 587-588 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

Shape unchanged; it should hold from 589, not 592: the Chen page has Jiankang taken in spring 589 (infobox 10 February 589) and the Chen shape ends in 589, not 591. 3.32 M km2 against the Sui infobox's 3.0 M km2 in 589 (ratio 1.11, fine). Beyond the Chen realm the shape adds about 0.29 M km2 of south-western uplands (bbox 101-112 E, 24-29.5 N) that no opened page dates or names: unverified: page budget.

602-608: adds the Red River delta around Hanoi (about 0.08 M km2 in the Cliopatria diff, bbox 104.6-107.9 E, 17.8-23 N), matching 'The Hanoi area was retaken from Lý Phật Tử in 602'. The shape is superseded from 609 by the Tuyuhun keyframe.

correction.text: the 602 Sui shape plus the Tuyuhun territory seized in 608 and toured in spring 609

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 609-611: Cliopatria draws no Sui gain from the Tuyuhun, but the Emperor Yang page has his forces 'seize Tuyuhun's territory, establishing four commanderies' (608) and a tour of 'the newly conquered Tuyuhun territory' in spring 609. The page does not locate the land, so Cliopatria's Tuyuhun 602 shape (0.55 M km2; 81.8-103.7 E, 32.8-41 N, the Qaidam and the Tarim edge, no overlap with the Sui) stands for it, as in the Tuyuhun dossier's matching 608 loss. The Tuyuhun page opened is silent on the conquest.

correction.text: the 602 shape without the Liaodong and North Korean land, plus the Tuyuhun territory

keyframe_review.note: Shape adjusted: Cliopatria adds about 0.08 M km2 (Liaodong and 28,000 km2 of North Korea, bbox 121.9-126.3 E, 38.9-41.7 N) for 612-616, but the Goguryeo-Sui War page gives 'Goguryeo victory', no territorial change, 'not a single castle, fortress, or citadel has fallen to Sui' in 612 and Sui forces withdrawn 'from Goguryeo's territory'. The correction is the 602 shape plus the Tuyuhun land of the 609 keyframe; the rebel-held land of 616 is carried by the ledger.

Shape unchanged, but only for 617. It already omits the Ordos (with the Yulin edge of northern Shaanxi) and Liaodong (the diff from 612 is 0.19 M km2), which matches Liang Shidu holding the Ordos 'by 617' (Transition page), yet it still shows Liu Wuzhou, Gao Kaidao, Li Mi, Dou Jiande, Xue Ju, Xiao Xian and Lin Shihong's land as Sui; the ledger's 616-617 loss events carve those. Li Yuan took Chang'an in winter 617.

correction.text: Luoyang, where Yang Tong was proclaimed after Emperor Yang's death, and from October 618 the Henan land retaken from Li Mi; held until summer 619

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 618-619: after Emperor Yang's death in spring 618, 'seven officials at Luoyang' made Yang Tong emperor; Sui officials held Luoyang until 'In summer 619, Wang Shichong had Yang Tong yield the throne to him'. The page gives the city, not a boundary; a 120 km radius, with Henan from October 618 (Wang Shichong's victory over Li Mi, land transfer bridged), is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: only the Ordos fragment (Liang Shidu's Liang) is a rival regime in 623-625; the rest of the 623 shape is Tang land

keyframe_review.note: Not Sui land: the Sui court ended in 618-619 and the Transition page says 'By this point [623], other than Liang Shidu and Gao Kaidao in the extreme north, China was largely reunited, if somewhat nominally, under Tang rule.' The 2.06 M km2 shape (gazetteer measure; Cliopatria 1.86 M km2) is the part of China outside Cliopatria's Tang 623 shape: the Tang's south plus the Ordos. Only the Ordos remnant is a rival regime. The Tang dossier must claim the rest.

correction.text: this shape is Liang Shidu's Liang, not the Sui; use it for liang-shidu-s-liang

keyframe_review.note: Not Sui: 0.11 M km2 in the Ordos and the bend of the Yellow River (bbox 106.6-112.5 E, 37.8-41.1 N) is Liang Shidu's Liang, which the Transition page has 'by 617' to 628 ('Liang Luoren killed Liang Shidu and surrendered' under Tang siege). Reassign to liang-shidu-s-liang.

correction.text: this shape is Liang Shidu's Liang, not the Sui; use it for liang-shidu-s-liang

keyframe_review.note: Same shape as 626 (109,171 km2): Liang Shidu's Liang, which survived to 628. Not the Sui.

region.text: the Northern Zhou realm, 'the former territory of the Northern Zhou' (3.59 million households in 580)

ledger.note: 581: Yang Jian ascends as Emperor Wen of Sui at Daxing. Infobox 'Ascension of Yang Jian: 4 March 581'; he 'usurped the throne from the Northern Zhou rulers' (the Northern Zhou page: 'On 4 March 581, Emperor Jing of Northern Zhou abdicated the throne in favor of Yang Jian, who changed the state name to Sui').

region.text: Jiangling and the Western Liang territory in central Hubei

ledger.note: 581: the Western Liang passes to the Sui's protection. The page's infobox calls it a 'Puppet state of Western Wei, Northern Zhou, and Sui dynasty' and says it 'remained a puppet state' throughout; the Northern Zhou's dossier ends the relation on 4 March 581.

region.text: Jiangling and the Western Liang territory in central Hubei

ledger.note: 587: the Sui ends the Western Liang's puppet status by abolishing it (see the gain below).

region.text: Jiangling and the Western Liang territory in central Hubei

ledger.note: 587: the Sui abolishes the Western Liang. Infobox 'Disestablished: 587 AD', 'Succeeded by: Sui dynasty'; the state 'was located in the middle Yangtze region in today's central Hubei province' and 'remained a puppet state'. The Chen page adds that in fall 587 two Western Liang officials surrendered to the Chen while the emperor was at the Sui court (see chen-dynasty).

region.text: the Yangtze front from Sichuan to the sea, where the Sui armies faced the Chen

ledger.note: 588: the Sui offensive on the Chen. The Sui page: in 588 it 'had amassed 518,000 troops along the northern bank of the Yangtze'; the Chen page: spring 588 a major attack, winter 588 three prongs under Yang Guang, with Yang Su coming down the upper Yangtze.

region.text: the Yangtze front, ended by the fall of Jiankang

ledger.note: 589: Jiankang falls. 'Spring 589: Heruo Bi crossed from Guangling, and Han Qinhu crossed at Caishi, sandwiching Jiankang'; Chen Shubao was found in a well and captured (the Chen infobox date is 10 February 589; the text says spring).

region.text: the Chen realm south of the Yangtze, from Jiankang to Lingnan

ledger.note: 589: the Sui reunify China. 'By 589, Sui troops entered Jiankang (now Nanjing) and the last emperor of Chen surrendered' (Sui page, infobox area 3,000,000 km2 in 589). The Lingnan and Jiaozhou submissions of 589-590 are on no opened page.

region.text: the steppe camps of the Qimin Khan's Turks under Sui protection (the page does not name them)

ledger.note: 600: the Sui backs the Qimin Khan of the Eastern Turks. 'Spring 600: Sui forces protected the Qimin Khan Ashina Rangan, whom Sui supported, from Ashina Dianjue's attack.' A client relation drawn as a tint; the page does not date his submission or locate his camp, so the steppe region is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Hanoi area, taken from Lý Phật Tử

ledger.note: 602: Sui retakes the Hanoi area. 'The Hanoi area was retaken from Lý Phật Tử in 602' (the last Early Lý ruler); the Linyi-Champa Campaign (602-605) follows.
605: the court moves from Daxing to Luoyang. Infobox 'Daxing (581-605), then Luoyang (605-618)'; the Emperor Yang page: in winter 604 he designated Luoyang the 'eastern capital'.

region.text: Tuyuhun's territory, where four commanderies were set up

ledger.note: 608: the Sui seize the Tuyuhun lands. Pei Ju set the Tiele on the Tuyuhun, 'forcing Tuyuhun's Busabuo Khan' Murong Fuyun to flee; Emperor Yang 'had his forces seize Tuyuhun's territory, establishing four commanderies, to be populated with exiles' and toured it in spring 609. The page does not locate the land or name the commanderies, so the Tuyuhun dossier's Cliopatria shape stands in; the Tuyuhun page is silent.

region.text: the Xiyu kingdoms whose rulers attended the audience at Zhangye

ledger.note: 609: the Western Regions come to Zhangye. 'Emperor Yang also received 27 rulers of Xiyu kingdoms in an audience at Zhangye' (spring 609): a tributary tint, not a conquest; the page names no protectorate and no end, so the end is bridged at the Sui collapse.

region.text: the Liao River and the Goguryeo fortresses east of it

ledger.note: 612: the Sui army crosses the Liao River against Goguryeo. 'The army began to depart in early 612'; of 305,000 men who crossed 'only 2,700 returned' after Salsu; 'not a single castle, fortress, or citadel has fallen to Sui' by June (infobox: 598, 612-614).

region.text: the Liao River and the Goguryeo fortresses east of it

ledger.note: 614: the war ends with no Sui gain. 'Emperor Yang accepted Yeongyang's offer of peace and withdrew Sui troops from Goguryeo's territory' after the 614 invasion; infobox result 'Goguryeo victory'; the 613 invasion of Liaodong had also been abandoned.

region.text: the steppe camps of the Qimin Khan's Turks

ledger.note: 615: the Turks turn on the Sui. Shibi Khan 'launched a surprise attack on Yanmen Commandery' and his army besieged the imperial train on 11 September 615.

region.text: central and eastern Henan without Luoyang

ledger.note: 617: Li Mi holds Henan as Duke of Wei. The Transition page has 'the rebels near Luoyang' coalescing under Li Mi in 616; the Li Mi page has Zhai Rang offer him 'the title of Duke of Wei' in spring 617 and says 'much of modern central and eastern Henan came under Li's rule' (infobox 617-618, 'Eastern Henan'). Luoyang itself stayed Sui.

region.text: the Ordos and the bend of the Yellow River, Cliopatria's 626 shape, which Cliopatria's 617 shape already drops

ledger.note: 617: Liang Shidu holds the Ordos. 'By 617, a number of other major rebel leaders also began to control significant portions of territory'; his Liang is based in 'central Inner Mongolia' and runs 'by 617' to 628. Cliopatria's 617 shape drops this land.

region.text: northern Shanxi, the page's 'modern northern Shanxi region', as a radius round Datong

ledger.note: 617: Liu Wuzhou holds northern Shanxi. His Dingyang state is 'in the modern northern Shanxi region', 'by 617' to summer 620.

region.text: the extreme north of Hebei, Cliopatria's Gao Kaidao shape

ledger.note: 617: Gao Kaidao holds northern Hebei. His Yan is in 'the modern extreme northern Hebei region', 'by 617' to 624.

region.text: Hebei north of the Yellow River, without Gao Kaidao's northern strip

ledger.note: 617: Dou Jiande holds the Hebei plain. The page has him 'further consolidated his holdings north of the Yellow River' and his Xia running c. 617-621; no month or boundary is given.

region.text: eastern Gansu (the Transition page adds western Shaanxi), as radii round Lanzhou and Tianshui

ledger.note: 617: Xue Ju holds eastern Gansu and western Shaanxi. His Qin lasted 'by 617' to 618, when Li Shimin defeated his son Xue Rengao and annexed it.

region.text: Baling Commandery and northern Hunan, his first base

ledger.note: 617: Xiao Xian rises at Baling. 'In 617, military officers at Baling Commandery (near modern Yueyang)' recruited him; he declared himself Duke of Liang at Luochuan and Prince of Liang in winter 617. The Transition page: Liang 'by 617' to 621.

region.text: Jiangxi and Guangdong, the span the page gives for Lin Shihong's Chu

ledger.note: 617: Lin Shihong holds Jiangxi and Guangdong. His Chu, 'in the modern Jiangxi and Guangdong region', existed 'by 617' and had dissolved before spring 623.

region.text: Chang'an and the Wei valley

ledger.note: 617: Li Yuan takes Chang'an. 'In winter 617, Li Yuan captured Chang'an, declaring Yang You emperor (as Emperor Gong)'; he founded the Tang there in 618.

region.text: the Tuyuhun territory seized in 608

ledger.note: 617: the Tuyuhun commanderies lapse. The pages opened say nothing about the end of the Sui hold on the Tuyuhun lands; bridged at the general collapse. The Tuyuhun page lists Busabo Khan Murong Fuyun to 635 and a Tang vassalage in 634; the Tuyuhun dossier dates 'Fuyun recovered' the lands to 619 from the Murong Fuyun page, which was not opened here.

region.text: Hubei, Guangxi and northern Vietnam, the rest of Xiao Xian's span

ledger.note: 618: Xiao Xian takes the middle Yangtze and the south. After summer 618 his general Yang Daosheng captured Jiangling, which became his capital; after Emperor Yang's death in spring 618, Sui officials in Guangxi and northern Vietnam 'largely surrendered' to him. His state covered 'most of modern Hubei, Hunan, Guangxi, and northern Vietnam'. The page gives no month.

region.text: the Xiyu kingdoms of the Zhangye audience

ledger.note: 618: the Western Regions' tributary tint ends with the Sui court; the pages opened date no end.

region.text: Chang'an and the Wei valley, the core of the new Tang; the rest of the empire divides among the rival regimes and Yang Tong's Luoyang

ledger.note: 618: Emperor Yang is assassinated and the empire breaks up. 'Emperor Yang was assassinated in 618' by Yuwen Huaji at Jiangdu (late spring); Li Yuan deposed Yang You and founded the Tang (infobox 'Abolished by Li Yuan: 23 May 618'); Luoyang officials proclaimed Yang Tong; Yuwen Huaji declared Yang Hao emperor, killed him later in 618 and proclaimed a brief Xu state.

region.text: central and eastern Henan, Li Mi's former holdings

ledger.note: 618: Wang Shichong crushes Li Mi and Li Mi's land comes over to the Luoyang court. 'Wang took this opportunity to launch a major attack on Li in fall 618' and beat him at Yanshi (October); afterwards 'most of Li's territory surrendered to Yang Tong's regime' (the rebel Zhu Can also submitted to it), while Xu Shiji's area went to the Tang. [Reviewer ea-03-f, 2026-10-19: raised from 1 to 2; the Wang Shichong page names the recipient]

region.text: Luoyang, where Yang Tong was proclaimed after Emperor Yang's death, and from October 618 the Henan land retaken from Li Mi; held until summer 619

ledger.note: 619: the last Sui regime yields to Wang Shichong. 'In summer 619, Wang Shichong had Yang Tong yield the throne to him', ending the Sui and founding the Zheng (to spring 621). Cliopatria's shapes for 620-627 are rival regimes and Tang land, not the Sui. [Reviewer ea-03-f, 2026-10-19: region set to the whole sui-dynasty_618 keyframe (Luoyang and Henan), which is what passed to the Zheng]

wars.name: Sui conquest of the Chen

zones.text: the Chen realm, entered from the Yangtze

wars.outcome: Sui victory: Jiankang taken in spring 589 and the last Chen emperor captured; the south joins the Sui.
wars.note: The Chen page has no separate article for the conquest.

wars.name: Goguryeo-Sui War

zones.text: the Liao River and the Goguryeo fortresses east of it

wars.outcome: Goguryeo victory; Sui withdrew in 614 holding no Goguryeo land and the losses 'contributed to the fall of the Sui dynasty'.
wars.note: The page describes no 598 campaign; invasions in 612, 613 and 614. Infobox lists the Eastern Turkic Khaganate on the Goguryeo side.

wars.name: Linyi-Champa Campaign

zones.text: the Hanoi area retaken from Lý Phật Tử in 602

wars.outcome: Sui retook the Hanoi area in 602 and won a battle against Cham war elephants, but 'many soldiers died of disease'.
wars.note: Dates and campaign name from the Sui page ('Linyi-Champa Campaign (602-605)'); the Emperor Yang page adds only that the conquest of Champa 'resulted in the death of thousands of Sui soldiers from malaria'. No Cham land is held.

wars.name: Sui conquest of the Tuyuhun
wars.outcome: Sui victory: Murong Fuyun fled and the Sui set up four commanderies; Emperor Yang toured the land in spring 609.

wars.name: Sui and the Turkic Khaganate
wars.outcome: The Sui split the Turkic Khaganate into Eastern and Western halves by diplomacy, protected the Qimin Khan in 600 and was attacked by Shibi Khan at Yanmen in 615.
wars.note: From and to are bounds, not dates of fighting: the Sui page gives no year for the split ('With Emperor Wen's diplomatic manoeuvre, the Khaganate split into Eastern and Western halves'); 600 and 615 are the Emperor Yang page's. No border moved.

wars.name: Sui rebellions and the Transition from Sui to Tang

zones.text: the Sui empire in revolt: 'in 611, in northern China, those who refused to be conscripted began to revolt as agrarian rebels'

wars.outcome: The Sui court fell in 618-619; the Tang beat the Xue, Liu, Wang, Dou, Xiao, Gao and Liang regimes between 618 and 628.
wars.note: Yang Xuangan rebelled and attacked Luoyang in 613 during the second Goguryeo campaign. Du Fuwei, Luo Yi, Li Zitong, Shen Faxing, Liu Heita and Fu Gongshi (623-624) also appear on the page and have no dossier here.

certainty.note: Frontiers with the steppe, Tarim, Tibetan plateau and Goguryeo are approximate; the Yangtze line to the Chen (581-588) and the 602 Red River frontier are the firmest edges but no treaty or survey fixes them; rebel-held land after 616 is drawn from named regions.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROWS. (1) The row starts in 587 but the Sui began on 4 March 581 (Sui infobox); 581-586 is drawn from the Northern Zhou 577 shape in new keyframe sui-dynasty_581, and the Northern Zhou dossier ends in 581. (2) The row runs to 627. The Sui court ended in 618-619 (Yang Tong yielded to Wang Shichong in summer 619), so the identity ends in 619 and the shapes of 620-627 are wrong as Sui: sui-dynasty_623 (623-625, 1.86 M km2) is the part of China outside Cliopatria's Tang 623 shape, i.e. Tang land in the south plus the Ordos; sui-dynasty_626 and _627 (109,171 km2) are Liang Shidu's Liang. The Tang dossier (ea-04) must claim the 623 shape's land. (3) The 612 shape's Liaodong and North Korean land is not supported: the Goguryeo-Sui War page records a Goguryeo victory and no Sui land ('The Goguryeo monarch Yeongyang gave up the buffer zone that he had acquired after the war of 598' and retreated behind the Liao River, without saying to whom; the Goguryeo dossier books that as a conf-1 loss to the Sui in 612, this dossier does not). (4) The 587 and 592 shapes should begin 587 and 589 respectively (Chen fell in Feb 589); 592 also draws about 0.29 M km2 of south-western uplands that no opened page names: unverified: page budget. (5) The 587 shape holds about 0.22 M km2 of the Ordos, northern Shanxi and northern Hebei not in the Northern Zhou shape; Cliopatria removes only the Ordos in 617 (the 617 ledger events carve northern Shanxi and Hebei).
PAGE BUDGET. Sui dynasty, Goguryeo-Sui War, Transition from Sui to Tang, Emperor Yang of Sui, Chen dynasty (shared with the Chen dossier), plus the Tuyuhun page which turned out silent: six pages. 'Sui conquest of the Chen' does not exist as an article (the URL returned not found) and the Chen page links none. Not opened and therefore not on the ledger: Emperor Wen of Sui (Sui-Turk wars 581-600, submission of Lingnan 589-590, the rebellions of the former Chen lands), the southwest, Ryukyu, Champa 605. A gap-filler should open 'Emperor Wen of Sui'.
REBEL STATES. The loss events of 616-617 and the 619 dissolve name the slugs of rebel-type dossiers written in this batch (li-mi-s-wei, dou-jiande-s-xia, wang-shichong-s-zheng, liang-shidu-s-liang, liu-wuzhou-s-dingyang, xue-ju-s-qin, xiao-xian-s-liang, lin-shihong-s-chu) and the Cliopatria row gao-kaidao (group ea-04). Du Fuwei (southern Anhui), Luo Yi (Beijing), Li Zitong's Wu (Jiangdu), Shen Faxing's Liang, Liu Heita's Handong, Lu (Xu Yuanlang) and Fu Gongshi's Song (623-624) need dossiers from another group; they are named on the Transition page but their land is not carved out of the Sui here. The regions for the 617 losses are readings of the page's modern-province spans ('by 617' is the regime's start, not each acquisition).
TUYUHUN. The 608 gain and the 617 loss use Cliopatria's Tuyuhun 602 shape, the same region as the Tuyuhun dossier's 608 loss; that dossier has the Tuyuhun recovering the land in 619 (Murong Fuyun page, not opened here), two years after this dossier's bridged loss. The Emperor Yang page does not name Xihai, Hezhou or the other commanderies.
TIBETAN, KOREAN AND SOUTHERN FRONTIERS. Early Lý (546-601) and Champa are neighbours in the seed; the Sui-Champa border is not drawn (no Cham land held). Counterpart 'Xiyu kingdoms (Western Regions)' has no dossier.
GAZETTEER. All names resolve with --resolve unless listed below.
